title: Drift-React: One-step Generation of Reaction Pathways via SE(3) Drifting Fields
claim: Existing approaches give isolated points or need thousands of iterative evaluations; ours produces the full pathway in one forward pass.
layout: 3 stacked rows, left-to-right, with a PES contour inset per row
description: A shared input on the left shows reactant and product molecules (X_R, X_P) joined by a bracket. Three horizontal rows branch from it. The top red dashed box is 'Point-wise Transition State Generators' (flow matching, diffusion), with icons listing 50–5,000 ODE/SDE steps, isolated TS with no pathway, and steric clashes. The middle orange dashed box is 'Iterative Path Relaxers' (NEB, NeuralNEB), with thousands of force evaluations and about 6–7 s per reaction. The bottom solid black box, 'Drift-React', is the largest. It shows a curved manifold M/SE(3) with a tangent plane and drift vectors, a joint affinity heatmap, and bullets for a single forward pass, 12–20 ms and a clash-free MEP. On the right, three contour-map insets show each outcome: a lone TS point, many orange relaxation iterates, and a smooth blue MEP. A small log-scale bar chart of NFE per inference sits at the bottom right.
caption: Three paradigms for reaction pathway prediction. Top: Point-wise generators (e.g., diffusion) predict isolated TS geometries at fast inference but ignore the surrounding PES valley, often producing structures with steric clashes. Middle: Iterative chain-of-states methods (e.g., NEB) recover the full MEP but require thousands of force evaluations per reaction. Bottom: Drift-React generates the complete reaction pathway in a single forward pass (∼12 ms) by learning an SE(3)- equivariant drifting field that balances target attraction with swarm repulsion.
abstract: Mapping reaction pathways and transition states (TS) is fundamental to chemistry but computationally expensive at scale. The minimum energy pathway (MEP) dictates reaction rates and mechanisms, yet recovering it via electronic-structure methods requires thousands of costly force evaluations. Recent generative models accelerate TS identification but rely on iterative inference and only predict isolated saddle-point snapshots, missing the continuous reaction trajectory. We introduce Drift-React, an $\mathrm{SE}(3)$-equivariant generative framework that predicts complete reaction pathways in a single forward pass from only reactant and product geometries. By shifting distribution evolution to training via a Sinkhorn-weighted drifting field, Drift-React eliminates both the iterative force evaluations of NEB-style methods and the sequential ODE/SDE integration of diffusion and flow matching models. Evaluated on the Transition1x and Halo8 datasets, our one-step model generates physically consistent MEPs that accurately capture energetic bottlenecks and enable arbitrary-resolution sampling along the reaction coordinate.
